content.value_statement: Multi-cloud planning is hard when teams compare AWS, Azure, and GCP without a shared framework. This skill provides service mappings, migration phases, cost guidance, and architecture patterns.
actual_capabilities: Compares common AWS, Azure, and GCP services for compute, storage, databases, and caching.
Explains four multi-cloud patterns, including disaster recovery, best-of-breed, geographic distribution, and cloud abstraction.
Outlines migration phases from assessment through optimization.
Lists cost optimization strategies across reserved capacity, spot capacity, rightsizing, serverless, and transfer costs.
Recommends cloud-agnostic building blocks such as Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, Redis, object storage APIs, and observability tools.
limitations: It provides architecture guidance, not provider-specific deployment code.
It does not calculate live pricing or current regional service availability.
It does not validate compliance requirements for a specific industry or jurisdiction.
It does not replace review by cloud security, networking, or finance specialists.

use_cases.title: Plan a Multi-Cloud Strategy
use_cases.description: Define provider roles, shared services, and portability goals before a major platform decision.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Migration Roadmap
use_cases.description: Break a provider migration into assessment, pilot, migration, and optimization phases.

use_cases.title: Compare Provider Services
use_cases.description: Map workload needs to AWS, Azure, and GCP services during technical design reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Provider Comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare AWS, Azure, and GCP options for my workload. Include compute, storage, database, cache, and monitoring choices.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Multi-Cloud Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a multi-cloud pattern for a customer-facing application with high availability, regional compliance, and moderate portability needs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Migration Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a phased migration plan from AWS to Azure with a pilot workload, dual-run period, rollback plan, and optimization tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Target Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed multi-cloud architecture for lock-in, resilience, cost risk, operational complexity, and missing observability controls.

output_examples.input: Compare service choices for a portable web application across AWS, Azure, and GCP.
output_examples.output: A provider comparison covering Kubernetes, managed SQL, Redis, object storage, monitoring, and tradeoffs for portability.

output_examples.input: Design a disaster recovery model that uses a second cloud provider.
output_examples.output: A primary-cloud and recovery-cloud pattern with replication, failover testing, operational ownership, and cost considerations.

output_examples.input: Plan a cloud migration for a business application.
output_examples.output: A phased roadmap with assessment, pilot, migration, monitoring, validation, and post-migration optimization steps.

best_practices: Start with workload requirements, compliance needs, and recovery targets before choosing providers.
Use infrastructure as code and standard observability across every cloud environment.
Test failover, rollback, data replication, and cost controls before production migration.
anti_patterns: Choosing multiple providers before defining the business reason for multi-cloud.
Mixing provider-specific services without an operations model for ownership and support.
Assuming service names are equivalent without validating limits, pricing, regions, and integration behavior.

faq.question: What cloud providers does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers AWS, Azure, and GCP service selection and architecture patterns.

faq.question: Can it help reduce vendor lock-in?
faq.answer: Yes. It highlights cloud-agnostic patterns using Kubernetes, common databases, open tools, and standard storage interfaces.

faq.question: Does it generate Terraform modules?
faq.answer: No. It recommends infrastructure as code practices, but it does not provide ready-to-run modules.

faq.question: Can it estimate exact monthly cloud costs?
faq.answer: No. It explains pricing factors and optimization strategies, but live cost estimates require provider pricing tools.

faq.question: Is this useful for disaster recovery planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a single-provider primary model with cross-cloud disaster recovery guidance.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
